answer_extracted:
Using Abel's theorem, \( W(t) = W(t_0) e^{-\int p(t)\,dt} \). Since \( W(t) \) is a non-zero constant, \( e^{-\int p(t)\,dt} \) is constant, implying \( \int p(t)\,dt \) is constant. Differentiating gives \( p(t) = 0 \).  
Thus, \( p(t) = 0 \).
